sections.h2: Selling in a city this size
sections.html:
Las Vegas fills a basin on the floor of the Mojave Desert, ringed by mountains, at about 2,000 feet above sea level. The city covers roughly 142 square miles, and the urban area around it runs to about 540. A house in Centennial Hills and one near Downtown can share a Las Vegas address and still be very different properties.

The neighborhoods include Summerlin, Queensridge, The Lakes, Rancho, Lone Mountain, Peccole Ranch and Canyon Gate, each with its own mix of build years, lot sizes and homeowners associations. Those traits shape what repairs a buyer will expect to see. Houses from different decades vary in roofing, windows, air conditioning and wiring, and the gaps drive the repair lists that make a traditional listing costly.

Tourism, gaming and conventions drive the local economy, so income can swing with visitor traffic and shift schedules. Owners who lose hours, relocate for work or inherit a house from a relative often have to sell on a timeline someone else set. A cash sale suits that situation because you and the buyer agree on the closing date instead of waiting for a lender to set it.

  • Job changes and relocation are common reasons for a quick sale.
  • Inherited houses often arrive with deferred maintenance and a pile of paperwork.
  • Landlords with tenants in place sometimes prefer a buyer who takes the property as it stands.

Summers here are long and extremely hot, with July highs averaging 104.5 degrees Fahrenheit and only about 4.2 inches of rain a year. Heat is hard on air conditioning, roof membranes, stucco, irrigation lines and pool equipment. An inspector will look at the age of the AC unit first. If it is near the end of its life, a buyer with a loan will usually ask for a credit or a replacement, which is a big reason sellers with older systems consider selling as-is.

Rain is rare but can arrive hard. The Clark County Regional Flood Control District was created in 1986 after a series of floods in the valley in the 1970s and early 1980s. Homeowner's insurance policies do not cover flood damage, and the county points owners to the National Flood Insurance Program. If a buyer's lender requires flood coverage on your parcel, that can come up late in the process.

Nevada requires a seller of residential property to complete the Real Estate Division's Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form, listing known conditions that materially affect the property. The statute is NRS 113.130, and the form is Form 547.

A buyer who closes without a completed form, or without being told of a known defect, may be entitled to treble damages unless the buyer waives that right under NRS 113.150(6). Answer the form honestly and in full.

Each deed presented to the county recorder must carry a declaration of value. NRS 375 allows the tax to be collected from either the buyer or the seller, so the contract should say who pays.

sections.h2: Can a house stay a short-term rental after a sale?
sections.html:
Not automatically, because the city sets eligibility rules for each new license. The City of Las Vegas defines a short-term residential rental as a house or condominium rented to guests for fewer than 31 consecutive days.

Under the city's 2026 instructions, a new license requires that the residence be at least 660 feet from any other short-term residential rental and 2,500 feet from a resort hotel, sit in a zone that allows the use, and have written HOA permission where an association exists. If you are selling a house that has been used as a rental, ask the Business Licensing Division what happens to the license at transfer, and tell buyers plainly what you know.

sections.h2: Clark County property tax when you sell
sections.html:
Clark County bills Las Vegas property tax. The full amount is due the third Monday in August, though owners can pay in installments when the tax on a parcel exceeds $100. The installments fall on the third Monday in August, then the first Mondays of October, January and March. The Treasurer mails real property tax bills only once each fiscal year, and owners who have not received one by August 1 can request a copy through the automated phone system. Late payments carry penalties under NRS 361.483, starting at 4 percent on a late installment.

If you disagree with your assessment, an appeal to the County Board of Equalization must be filed on or before January 15. Owner-occupants also have a partial abatement under NRS 361.4723 that keeps a primary residence's tax increase near 3 percent a year, and the statute excludes homes rented to others.

sections.h2: What a cash sale looks like
sections.html:
A cash sale means the buyer is not relying on a mortgage, so there is no lender appraisal or underwriting to wait on. The usual steps are an offer, a title search, the seller's disclosure form, a signed contract, a closing with a title or escrow company, and a deed and declaration of value presented for recording.

Your own timeline depends on the condition of title, any liens, whether tenants occupy the house and how quickly the HOA, if there is one, answers requests for documents. Cash Home Buyers does not promise a specific price. We look at the house as it is, and you can decline an offer without owing anything.

sections.h2: What Las Vegas sellers usually face
sections.html:
These situations often make a conventional listing hard.

  • An aging air conditioning system, roof or pool that would draw repair requests.
  • An inherited house that needs probate or a transfer on death deed to be completed first.
  • A tenant in place, or a rental with an unclear short-term license.
  • HOA documents, assessments or violations that must be sorted before closing.
  • A loan balance, tax installment or other lien that needs to be paid at closing.

Each of these can be handled in a cash sale, though the order of operations varies. Gather your deed, the latest tax bill, any HOA statements and the mortgage payoff before you talk to a buyer, and the process moves faster.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax when I sell a house in Las Vegas?
faqs.a: $2.55 for every $500 of value in Clark County, made up of the $1.95 state rate plus a $0.60 county add-on. NRS 375 lets either side be charged, so the contract decides who pays.

faqs.q: Do I have to fill out a seller disclosure in Nevada?
faqs.a: Yes. A residential seller must complete the Real Estate Division's Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form under NRS 113.130. A buyer who closes without it, or without being told of a known defect, may be entitled to treble damages unless that right was waived.

faqs.q: When are Clark County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The third Monday in August. Parcels with taxes over $100 can be paid in four installments, with the others on the first Monday of October, January and March.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Las Vegas property assessment?
faqs.a: Until January 15, with a petition to the Clark County Board of Equalization. A weekend or holiday on that date moves the deadline to the next business day.

faqs.q: Does the turf removal law force me to tear out my grass before selling?
faqs.a: No, not for a single-family home. The Southern Nevada Water Authority says the law, which bars Colorado River water on nonfunctional grass from 2027, covers commercial, multi-family, government and other properties and does not apply to grass in single-family yards.
